problem: The unit statement is backwards. A rate written in µm/s has a numerical value 60 times smaller than the same rate in µm/min, so the etching time comes out 60 times larger when expressed in seconds (not 60 times smaller). As written, a student who follows the trap will move the decimal the wrong way.
fix: Say: "A rate in µm/s is 60 times smaller as a number than the same rate in µm/min, so the time you compute is in seconds and is 60 times the time in minutes. Convert every rate and time to the same units before dividing." Example: 1.4 µm/min = 0.0233 µm/s; 300 µm takes 214.3 min = 12 857 s.

problem: The answer says "the pit widens as it goes down", which contradicts Section 2 ("A pit is wider at the top than at the bottom"). The conclusion is right but the stated reason is the opposite of the geometry, so a student revising from the answer learns the wrong shape.
fix: "The (111) sidewalls slope at 54.7° to the surface, so the pit is widest at the mask opening and narrows as it goes down. The mask opening must therefore be larger than the final diaphragm by the sidewall run-out on each side, about 0.71 × depth (about 212 µm per side for a 300 µm pit); otherwise the diaphragm comes out smaller than designed."

where: Quiz Q5 (and the deposition table in Section 3)
problem: The question asks for two deposition methods, but the answer gives thermal oxidation, which grows oxide by consuming silicon rather than depositing a film. The chapter itself says this in Section 3, so the answer and the table row quietly label growth as deposition. Only one true deposition method (sputtering) is offered.
fix: Answer: "LPCVD deposits polysilicon; sputtering deposits aluminium." If the table is kept as a general film-formation list, add a note against the thermal oxidation row: "growth, not deposition — consumes the silicon surface".
